label: Dry spell broken by a sharp burst
why_this_case_matters: Totals alone are misleading; the key is the sudden break after dryness.
why_this_window_length: The story is the break, not the total.
facts_to_read: Rain 81.1mm vs 24.8mm normal | avg high dev -1.8°C | avg low dev +0.1°C | rainy days 10 | wettest 3-day stretch 51.7mm | antecedent dry streak 51 days | record days 0
your_headline: Over 20mm rain each on 24/25 Apr, leading to sharp drop in temperatures
what_claude_should_learn: There is not really a "sustained dry spell" but the heavy rain on 23/24 is the real story here. And ther is a drop in temperature as well (compared to normal) which neesd to be highlighted

label: Sustained wet stretch
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model to recognise persistence rather than a single heavy day.
why_this_window_length: A longer window is needed so the persistence is visible.
facts_to_read: Rain 361.0mm vs 132.6mm normal | avg high dev -0.9°C | avg low dev +0.4°C | rainy days 30 | wettest 3-day stretch 69.7mm | antecedent dry streak 0 days | record days 0
your_headline: Consistently heavy rain through all of October. No dry days! Over 30mm burst on 27th led to sharp temperature drop
what_claude_should_learn: Real signal here is - rained every single day. And the cold bursts it produced.

label: Rain concentrated into one short spell
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model not to call a window broadly wet when the rain is concentrated.
why_this_window_length: Shorter framing prevents one burst from being misread as a wet fortnight.
facts_to_read: Rain 110.7mm vs 24.5mm normal | avg high dev +0.8°C | avg low dev +0.6°C | rainy days 3 | wettest 3-day stretch 110.6mm | antecedent dry streak 5 days | record days 0
your_headline: Extreme rain (~80mm) on May 20, coming off hot dry spell earlier in the week
what_claude_should_learn: First part of this data is mostly hot and dry. Then rain starts and ramps up. B ut the real story here is  very heavy rain on 20th

label: Persistently dry window
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model to treat absence of rain as a real signal.
why_this_window_length: A wider window is useful because absence is cumulative.
facts_to_read: Rain 1.1mm vs 57.7mm normal | avg high dev +2.7°C | avg low dev +0.3°C | rainy days 1 | wettest 3-day stretch 1.0mm | antecedent dry streak 0 days | record days 9
your_headline: Dry spell from 13-25 Oct. Just 1mm rain vs 58mm expected
what_claude_should_learn: WE highlight both the length of the dry spell and the aggregates. Makes the story more powerful

label: Daytime heat spell
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model to prioritise a clear daytime heat run.
why_this_window_length: The run-length matters more than any single hottest day.
facts_to_read: Rain 3.4mm vs 34.8mm normal | avg high dev +4.4°C | avg low dev +3.6°C | rainy days 5 | wettest 3-day stretch 2.5mm | antecedent dry streak 12 days | record days 11
your_headline: Sustained heat wave for past 2 weeks - both maximum and minimum temperatures over 3 degrees over normal
what_claude_should_learn: Just focus on the heat story here while there is a dryness story as well.

label: Warm-night run
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model not to miss elevated night temperatures when highs are less dramatic.
why_this_window_length: This needs enough days for the night pattern to be unmistakable.
facts_to_read: Rain 13.6mm vs 9.9mm normal | avg high dev +1.5°C | avg low dev +3.7°C | rainy days 11 | wettest 3-day stretch 7.8mm | antecedent dry streak 8 days | record days 3
your_headline: Sustained warm spell this winter, with minimum temperatures 4 degrees above normal. Rain failed to break hot spell
what_claude_should_learn: In Bangalore usually rain brings temperature down. Here, =despite winter raijn, tempereaatures reimained elevated and that's worth calling out

label: Cool daytime spell
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model to spot sustained cool highs relative to normal.
why_this_window_length: This is about persistent daytime coolness, not a one-day dip.
facts_to_read: Rain 129.5mm vs 8.6mm normal | avg high dev -4.5°C | avg low dev -0.6°C | rainy days 14 | wettest 3-day stretch 43.5mm | antecedent dry streak 3 days | record days 0
your_headline: Unseasonal heavy rains lead to rather cool March. Highs 5 degrees below normal
what_claude_should_learn: Ther is an alternate story of how March that year was rather rainy. Hardly rains in March. But t emperature is the bigger story

label: Cool-night run
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model to separate cool nights from cool days.
why_this_window_length: The window is chosen to preserve the night-time pattern.
facts_to_read: Rain 1.8mm vs 54.7mm normal | avg high dev +0.9°C | avg low dev -3.6°C | rainy days 1 | wettest 3-day stretch 1.8mm | antecedent dry streak 0 days | record days 9
your_headline: Cold nights and no rain since Oct27. Lows 3.5 degr below expected.
what_claude_should_learn: Both the cold and the dryness are strong stories for this eime of the year, b u the cold is the more interesting story

label: Record-heavy patch
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model to foreground records when they cluster.
why_this_window_length: The record cluster is the editorial hook.
facts_to_read: Rain 0.6mm vs 25.8mm normal | avg high dev +3.8°C | avg low dev -0.1°C | rainy days 2 | wettest 3-day stretch 0.6mm | antecedent dry streak 2 days | record days 14
your_headline: Record high temperatures (4 degrees above normal) for the last 14 days. Hot  and dry November!
what_claude_should_learn: The number of days of records is interesing here. When it is close to the overall number of days it takes precedence in terms of the sotry.

label: Wet month building through accumulation
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model that some stories are cumulative and need a month-long frame.
why_this_window_length: A 30-day view is needed because the anomaly accumulates.
facts_to_read: Rain 371.5mm vs 56.6mm normal | avg high dev -0.8°C | avg low dev +2.1°C | rainy days 25 | wettest 3-day stretch 169.8mm | antecedent dry streak 0 days | record days 1
your_headline: Wet November, primarily driven by deluge on 15/16. 370mm rain vs 57mm expected
what_claude_should_learn: This is not sustained. The main story is that ther are 2 days that really contributed to the wet patch. So it's not an accumulation storyy here.

label: Dry month building through accumulation
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model that rainfall deficits often need a month-long frame.
why_this_window_length: A 30-day view is needed because the deficit builds gradually.
facts_to_read: Rain 27.2mm vs 138.0mm normal | avg high dev +1.9°C | avg low dev +0.0°C | rainy days 9 | wettest 3-day stretch 22.5mm | antecedent dry streak 0 days | record days 6
your_headline: Only 27 mm rain in the last month, compared to 136mm usual (20%!). Rather dry October
what_claude_should_learn: One rainy day in this period versus usual _ is another storye we can talk about.

label: Heat-to-rain whiplash
why_this_case_matters: This teaches the model to keep two linked signals in view instead of flattening them.
why_this_window_length: The chosen span keeps both parts of the story visible.
facts_to_read: Rain 11.0mm vs 7.3mm normal | avg high dev +0.8°C | avg low dev +0.3°C | rainy days 4 | wettest 3-day stretch 10.9mm | antecedent dry streak 60 days | record days 5
your_headline: Rains from 10Mar led to sharp drop in temperature after record hot period
what_claude_should_learn: It's a little difficult to communicate here - the big rain was on 12th, but 10th onwards it was cool.
